All four figures were measured by parsing PLACEHOLDER_POPULATION_TABLE_R13.md's 3264 data rows at git pin c05f9f9fc9 (never the working tree, which the sibling cell regenerates this round) and counting, per row, how many of the 9 known placeholder tokens ({system}/{scope}/{cadence}/{source}/{snap}/{dim_name}/{firm}/{d}/{dc}) occur in that row's `canonical` column. by_token_sum (1449) and rows_with_a_placeholder (1303) recomputed this way match PLACEHOLDER_POPULATION_R13.json's own tokens.by_token[].rows sum and population.rows_with_a_placeholder exactly, at the same pin, from a DIFFERENT artifact (the row-level table vs the pre-aggregated json) -- corroboration, not repetition. rows_carrying_more_than_one (138) was measured the same way (count of rows whose per-row token-type count exceeds 1), NEVER computed as sum-rows (146): the instrument-vs-inference distinction is stated in the record's own `instrument.measured_by` field, and the difference between 138 and 146 (8) is exactly the 8 rows carrying three tokens each over-contributing a second excess unit to sum-rows -- the order's own warning ('sum - rows is NOT the count of multi-token rows ... equals the multi-token row count only when no row carries three or more') is demonstrated live in this data, not merely quoted. The distribution {1:1165, 2:130, 3:8} was read by subtraction from the 1303-row denominator (1165+130+8=1303) per Rule 24, not as a forward list of expected multiplicities -- 3 was not assumed in advance, it was found.
